key_insight: ECG and patient metadata supported classification of broad NT-proBNP concentration ranges, with 12-lead ECG outperforming lead II alone, while precise concentration prediction remained challenging.
clinical_relevance: ECG-based NT-proBNP estimates may offer complementary information about cardiovascular processes but cannot replace laboratory measurements.
method: Multimodal deep learning combined ECG recordings with patient metadata.
Compared lead II alone with 12-lead ECG using MIMIC-IV data.
Evaluated regression, binary classification, and three-class classification using clinically established thresholds.
evidence_signal: For 1-lead versus 12-lead ECG, regression MAE was 534.98 versus 514.27 pg/mL, binary AUROC was 0.849 versus 0.876, and three-class macro-AUROC was 0.738 versus 0.752.
watch_item: Independent-dataset validation is needed before considering clinical implementation.
paper_title: ECG for laboratory values:A comprehensive physiological and technical analysis
